section_summary: This section concludes several Shanghai case files on Filipino residents accused of collaborating with Japanese authorities. The files combine the subjects’ own accounts with statements from other Filipinos, membership records, petitions, and newspaper extracts; many allegations are contested. The final pages shift to a report on John Henry Turner and the opening of a field report on a Japanese intelligence network in southern China.

subfiles.title: Valentine Punsalan case file, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Statements and records concerning Punsalan's alleged support for Japanese-sponsored Filipino organisations.
subfiles.summary: The closing pages cite his signatures on association rolls and petitions, his alleged false claim to the Swiss Consulate that he had refused allegiance, and statements by Evangelista and Lucero describing contacts with Japanese gendarmes.

subfiles.title: Details concerning Romiro Quamson
subfiles.about: A biographical note describes a Filipino musician in Tianjin as a Japanese collaborator.
subfiles.summary: Records Quamson's movements, family, association office and nightclub work.

subfiles.title: Armando J. Sales
subfiles.doc_type: intelligence case report with signed statements
subfiles.about: Sales's account of wartime Filipino politics in Shanghai is assessed against accusations from other witnesses.
subfiles.summary: Sales asserts loyalty to the Philippine Commonwealth, describes Japanese pressure and hardship, and requests a compulsory meeting to investigate accusations. Evangelista, Canlas and Espino instead identify him as Contreras's active associate. The report also cites Sales's signatures on Japanese-sponsored association rolls and petitions.

subfiles.title: F. Salvador
subfiles.doc_type: intelligence case report with signed statements
subfiles.about: Salvador's explanation for signing Japanese-sponsored documents is compared with former prisoners' accusations.
subfiles.summary: Salvador says Kalambakal brought him before Japanese officers and induced him to sign papers. Extracts from Espino, Rosete and Canlas describe affidavits used against pro-American Filipinos and their interrogations and beatings. The report adds Salvador's participation in ceremonies and petitions, while Evangelista calls him a pro-Japanese follower of Kalambakal.

subfiles.title: Victorino Tulio
subfiles.doc_type: intelligence case report with signed statements
subfiles.about: Tulio explains his wartime allegiance while witnesses describe his alleged pro-Japanese speeches and activities.
subfiles.summary: Tulio says he answered yes to the allegiance question to protect his family. The report records his association membership and independence ceremony participation. Evangelista, Canlas, Gonzaga and Lucero provide accounts of praise for Japan and anti-American remarks.

subfiles.title: Conrado Uy: wartime activities and witness statements
subfiles.about: Uy gives a lengthy defence of his wartime journalism and association work, followed by accounts disputing it.
subfiles.summary: Uy describes founding the Filipino Association, disputes Kalambakal's methods, explains the allegiance registration and relief efforts, and defends his writing as support for Philippine independence. He says reports of Japanese atrocities later changed his views. Espino, Evangelista, Alobog, Malabanan and Alindada allege intimidation, propaganda and links to Japanese authorities; their statements differ from Uy's account.

subfiles.title: Conrado Uy: supplementary details and press extracts
subfiles.about: Newspaper extracts and witness statements document Uy's public advocacy and alleged recruitment activities.
subfiles.summary: The supplement quotes 1942–43 Shanghai Times and Filipino Clarion articles promoting Japanese-backed Philippine independence and criticising the United States. It reproduces a petition to Tojo and statements alleging that Uy pressured musicians and proposed intelligence work in Manila. Paul Aquino describes a Japanese-sponsored trip to Nanjing.

subfiles.title: John Henry Turner
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Shanghai
subfiles.about: A report alleges that Turner worked for Japanese interests during the war.
subfiles.summary: Summarises allegations of Japanese employment and intelligence work; requests attention to Turner's case.

subfiles.title: The Japanese South China Intelligence Group Five Provinces Information Department
subfiles.from: Jason Paige Jr., Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Paige forwards a field report prepared in Guangzhou on a Japanese intelligence group.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a field report dated 29 September 1945 and notes its B-2 evaluation.

subfiles.title: The Japanese South China Intelligence Group Five Provinces Information Department
subfiles.about: The report describes the group's origins, offices, structure and suspected personnel.
subfiles.summary: The report attributes the group's establishment in Guangzhou to Doihara and Okubo and lists branch offices across southern China. It identifies headquarters, espionage, communications and propaganda sections, then profiles Okubo, the Fok brothers and Li Pei Lo. The espionage section profiles Chan Chi Kong, executed agent Chan Wai Hung and Yang Wai; the report continues beyond this section.
